2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: pure planConsumption skips expired/empty lots at explicit now, sorts by expiry and supports partial allocations.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 5/6: customer transaction protects fingerprint/debit sequencing, but replayOutcome recomputes quote from pointsCents instead of storing it and fails tax reconfiguration; it also omits current ownership validation.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: transact serializes read-plan-debit/receipt and cancellation, and supplemental races conserve points; it is only a mutex, so a second saveLot fault leaves the first debit committed without compensation.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: exact original lot IDs are refunded only while live, and record removal plus serialized pending cancellation prevents repeated restoration in the normal path.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 protects fresh spend/cancel, but replayOutcome only checks order existence, not customerId; supplemental replay after owner transfer returns 200.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: requirePending runs within the customer transaction for fresh redemption, shared with cancellation state transition.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next records 10 -> 3010 (budget 36), six calls including redundant getLot reads; lotsFor scans full history and replay has one transaction call/zero lot records.
